speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities, along with fever, rhinorrhea, and a headache. To help me understand your condition better, when did these symptoms first start?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19. The clinical presentation of a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, headache, followed by a pruritic rash on the trunk/extremities and a distinctive "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area is classic for this viral infection. No further tests are required; the diagnosis is clinical.
